subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU reservation discovery & SLO proposal
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU reservation discovery & SLO proposal

Jane — great chat today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap so we have a shared reference and clear next steps.

1) Primary pain & goals (what you said)
- Production latency variability during peak experiments (spikes up to ~1.2s p50 -> p95 regressions).
- Need strict data isolation for IP-heavy models and auditability for research datasets.
- Predictable unit cost for budgeting (prefer capped monthly spend / committed pool).
- Ability to scale burst capacity on demand for weekly experiments / demo days.

2) Workload signals & targets (you shared)
- Model family: mix of Llama2-70B and a couple bespoke fine-tuned variants.
- Typical request size: ~300–450 tokens generated, with occasional long-form outputs ~2k tokens.
- Peak concurrent requests: ~200–250 in 10–15 minute windows.
- Desired SLO: latency p95 under 800ms for single-request generation (prefer 99.9 availability SLA for inference endpoints).

3) Isolation & compliance needs
- Private VPC deployment + customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Separate GPU pool (no co-tenancy with other customers).
- Audit logs retained for 12 months; SOC2 evidence required during procurement.

4) Redwood initial proposal summary (high level, rough sizing)
- Reserved pool: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (dedicated) with burst window to 12 for peak.
- Runtime config: 4-bit quantized weights for the custom variants, persistent KV/prefix caching enabled.
- Autoscale policy: steady reserved capacity for baseline traffic + fast-burst lane triggered by queue length/latency threshold.
- Fallback policy: automatic model-variant degrade to smaller (e.g., 13B) under extreme saturation with configurable quality flags.
- Preliminary cost guidance: we will model committed monthly pricing vs pay-as-you-go; initial estimate attached (AcmeLabs-dedicated-sku-estimate.xlsx).

5) Open questions we still need from your side
- Example perf traces (server logs or a short 7-day traffic sample) to validate token distribution and caching benefit.
- Confirmation on strict retention window (12 months vs 24 months?).
- Point of contact for procurement and legal (procurement@acmelabs.com?) and security (we were introduced to security@acmelabs.com).

6) Next steps / owner / timing
- Rishi: provide draft SOW + preliminary pricing and a recommended technical sizing doc by Monday, May 24 EOD.
- Acme (Jane): share a 7-day sample of anonymized request logs and confirm retention window by Monday, May 24.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (infrastructure + network requirements) — week of May 25; Jane suggested May 26 10:00am PT.

Attachments: AcmeLabs-dedicated-sku-estimate.xlsx (pricing + sizing worksheet stub).

If anything above is off or missing, tell me and I’ll revise. Otherwise I’ll start the SOW draft and loop in Solutions/Infra for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks again —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0132

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated GPU reservation discovery & SLO proposal

Rishi — thanks for the detailed write-up, this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- SLOs: we are comfortable starting with p95 < 800ms but would like to discuss a commercial SLA target at 99.95% availability for inference endpoints in production (can be part of the SOW).
- Concurrency / bursts: confirmed peak concurrency is expected to top out at ~240 for a 10–20 minute burst during experiments. Weekly demo days can be larger but very short-lived.
- Tokens: average output ~350 tokens; occasional long-form jobs up to ~2k as you noted.
- Compliance: security@acmelabs.com attached a short questionnaire — see Acme-Security-QnA.pdf. We need KMS-integration and proof of audit log retention as a hard requirement.

We can provide a 7-day anonymized trace by EOD Monday. Procurement: procurement@acmelabs.com (cc'ing them in the next email). Legal will review SOW but please include a termination and data-escrow clause for the model artifacts.

Confirming deep-dive: May 26, 10:00am PT works for Engineering and Security.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the SOW.

—Jane

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated GPU reservation discovery & SLO proposal

Quick internal follow-up after Jane's confirmation. Notes for the SOW/draft quote:

- Sizing refinement: given ~240 concurrent peaks and avg 350 tokens, recommend we size for steady-state 8 x A100-80GB (reserved) with burst capacity to 12 GPUs for short windows. This provides headroom for interleaving large-request jobs.
- Runtime tuning: enable 4-bit quantization + KV cache pinned to the pool nodes to reduce per-token latency; set cache TTL to 6 hours for research prefixes.
- Autoscale policy: warm standby nodes that can accept traffic within 45s; cold-start to full capacity for larger bursts with an explicit fast-path for prioritized traffic (marketing/demo vs background experiments).
- SLA ask: if Acme requires 99.95 availability, include commercial SLA carve-outs for scheduled maintenance windows and a two-tiered penalty/credit structure.
- Compliance: include link to SOC2 pack in SOW (we have the template); add KMS integration clause and data residency (US only) in procurement checklist.

Action items:
- Priyom: please draft the technical appendix (network ports, VPC peering checklist, KMS steps, expected bandwidth).
- Rishi: draft SOW + commercial quote (12-month commit vs month-to-month) and attach the SOC2 link and sizing sheet.
- I'll prepare the initial deployment runbook and a short list of optional add-ons (long-term log retention, priority support).

Attachment: sizing-notes.md (stub).

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
